text:
alex: heads up — ran a microbenchmark trying the packed/interleaved KV layout with our paged Flash variant and I see a weird p99 regression for short seqs (<=32).

maya: ugh. numbers?

alex: baseline (separate kv) on A100: q8, batch=16, seq=16 -> 1.8ms p50 / 3.2ms p99.
packed/interleaved -> 2.1ms p50 / 5.6ms p99. throughput drops ~12%.

ranjit: that p99 jump is big. did you run with the same kernel selection policy? could be falling back to non-fused path after alignment mismatch.

alex: kernel selection identical — policy picked flash-paged-fused for both. I captured profiler traces and saw extra memcopies near page boundaries.

alex: snippet from nvprof timeline:
```
memcpy H2D  128KB  (aligned to page boundary)  <-- spikes at input partition edges
kernel: flash_paged_fused_kv  (oversubscribed grid)  <- longer wait times
memcpy D2H  4KB   (kv tail)  <-- lots of small transfers
```

sara: small transfers smell like stride/dtype mismatch. are we padding to 128B alignment? packed layout reduced stride so tail fragments are crossing 4KB pages?

alex: exactly. packed reduces per-head stride to 16B * seq_len, so for seq=16 heads that fits awkwardly inside our page chunking. When a request boundary hits a page edge we end up issuing dozens of tiny transfers to assemble the page cache.

maya: did you try forcing 128B alignment or rounding strides up? That would add memory but might avoid memcopy churn.

alex: I tried a quick experiment: round stride up to 128B for kv pages only, same q8 settings. p99 improved to 3.4ms vs 5.6ms, p50 2.0ms. throughput recovered ~6% but peak GPU memory went up ~3%.

ranjit: tradeoff seems promising. Another axis: batching heuristics. If we bias the batcher to avoid mixing tiny seq requests that cause page boundary churn, we might keep packed layout and reduce copies. Did you profile with mixed seq distributions?

alex: yes — mixed load (seqs 8/16/64) made it worse: pack layout + mixed -> p99 up to 7.2ms. Seems boundary friction is worse when the prefix alignment varies between requests in the same micro-batch.

sara: maybe we need two mitigations: 1) kernel-level: detect page-crossing and coalesce transfers inside kernel (defer copies until whole page assembled), 2) batching-level: add an alignment-aware batching heuristic that groups requests by kv-page offset mod page_size.

maya: alignment-aware batching sounds feasible. We already compute hash offsets for routing; we can add a secondary key: page_offset = (start_pos * head_stride) % PAGE_BYTES. Then prefer micro-batches with similar offsets.

ranjit: good idea. It might increase latency for some requests due to queuing, but should reduce expensive memcpys. We can make it opt-in behind a flag and try in dedicated pools.

alex: infra-bot ran the perf run I requested and posted raw traces: https://perf/reports/1767554321 (internal). Highlights: memcopy count per forward went from 3 -> 28 for worst-case micro-batch.

infra-bot: benchmark run completed: 2000 iters, model: redwood-small, hardware: A100-40GB, config: q8 + packed-kv. Attached flamegraph id: fg-1767554321.

maya: for kernel fix, we can also examine dtype width. q8 uses 1 byte per weight but our KV cache math uses 2-byte staging in some paths to avoid divergence. If we standardize to byte-packed paths end-to-end we might eliminate temporary memcpy/convert steps. Anyone tried forcing no-conversion path?

alex: forced byte-path eliminated ~30% of the small-copy operations but didn't fully cure page-boundary copies. The conversion avoidance helps but page crossing still triggers D2H/H2D glue.

sara: what about padding policy: keep packed layout but ensure each page holds an integral number of heads (round heads per page). That keeps offsets consistent and prevents tail fragments. Cost: small wasted space per page.

ranjit: calculate cost: page=4KB, head_stride ~ (kV_len * head_width). For 32 heads, rounding means maybe 1-2 heads wasted per page -> memory overhead ~ head_size * wasted_heads * num_layers. For redwood-small that seems acceptable. For huge models we need better heuristics.

alex: next steps I propose:
- implement optional stride-rounding to 128B + head-aligned pages (kernel side quick patch).
- prototype alignment-aware batching policy (batcher change + opt-in config).
- run full sweep: seq lengths [8,16,32,64], batch sizes [8,16,32], q8/q4 variants.

maya: I'll pick up the batching patch (opt-in flag: align_batching=true).

ranjit: I'll prototype kernel-side page coalescing and stride rounding.

alex: thanks — if we can get p99 within 1.3-1.5x of separate-kv we can keep packed layout as default in dedicated pools. leaving notes in the perf doc. :thumbsup:

sara: also add metric in console: kv-memcopy-count and kv-page-fragment-rate so we can alert if this spikes in prod.

alex: good call. I'll add the telemetry PR after we validate.

maya: rough timeline? aiming to land both patches in 1 week for canary.

alex: sounds good. I'll coordinate canary runs.

ranjit: fyi I traced a small potential regression in fused kernel launch params when rounding strides — might need grid dim clamp. Will include that check.

alex: perfect. thanks folks.

maya: thanks — ping me when you drop the batching flag so I can flip it in the canary cluster. :rocket:
